la:adj:omnis.html:
omnĭs, e (omnia is freq. a dissyl. in the poets, as ; ; Lachm.), adj.
etym. dub.; perh. akin to ambo and Gr. ἀμφί
(syn.: cunctus, universus),
all, every: omnium rerum, quas ad beate vivendum sapientia comparaverit, nihil esse majus amicitiā,: ego nulli omnium neque populorum neque regum ... non ausim me comparare,: nemo omnium imperatorum, qui vivunt,.—With sup.: cur, si cuiquam novo civi potuerit adimi civitas, non omnibus antiquissimis civibus possit, all, even of the oldest families, Cic. Caecin. 35, 101: id effugiet qui non omnia minima repetet,.—Cf. with etiam: ut omnium tibi auxilia adjungas, etiam infimorum,: omnibus tuis etiam minimis commodis, Treb. Pol. ap. ; : Nero ad omnes etiam minimos Circenses commeabat,.—But with summa, extrema, and ultima, the neutr. plur. omnia is often closely connected in a distributive sense (= quidquid summum, etc.): a te, qui nobis omnia summa tribuis,: sed is omnia summa sperans aedilicius est mortuus,: constituit extrema omnia experiri,: quod omnia ultima pati quam se regi tradere maluissent,: omnes omnium ordinum homines,: omnibus precibus petere contendit,with prayers of every kind, most urgently,.—Esp. as subst.
omnes, ium, comm., all men, all persons: quis est omnium, qui? etc.,: unus ex omnibus,.—With gen. part.: Macedonum omnes,: praetorum, nisi qui inter tumultum effugerunt, omnes interficiuntur,; cf. ; cf. also: ut omnes Tarquiniae gentis exules essent,: omnes Hernici nominis,.—
omnĭa, ĭum, n., all things: omnium nomine quicumque ludos faciunt, etc.,: omnia facere,to do every thing, make every exertion, spare no pains,: omnia fore prius arbitratus sum, quam, etc., I should have believed any thing rather than that, etc., : omnia mihi sunt cum aliquo, I agree with him on all topics, in all points (but mihi omnia communia sunt is the better read., Baiter), : in eo sunt omnia,every thing depends on that,: omnia, quae sunt ad vivendum necessaria,; ; : omnia, quaecumque agimus,: esse omnia alicui,to be one's all,: Demetrius iis unus omnia est,: per omnia,in all points, in every thing, in every respect,: vir alioqui per omnia laudabilis,: plebes omnia quam bellum malebat,; ; cf. : eadem omnia, just the same: mihi certum est efficere in me omnia eadem, quae tu in te faxis,: alia omnia, just the contrary: te alia omnia, quam quae velis, agere, moleste ferrem,; cf. alius, 6: omnia, adverbially, altogether, entirely, in every respect: tramites, omnia plani et ex facili mobiles,: omnia Mercurio similis,in all respects,.—
In sing., every, all, the whole: militat omnis amans,every lover, all lovers,: quia sine omni malitiā'st, without any (colloq. for sine ullā), ; so, sine omni periclo,; but: ne sine omni quidem sapientiā,not without all knowledge, a complete philosophy,: cum omnis honestas manet a partibus quattuor,: materia ad omnem laudem, et publice, et privatim, etc.,every kind of,: castra plena omnis fortunae publicae privataeque,: cenare holus omne,every kind of,: Gallia est omnis divisa in partes tres,the whole of Gallia,; cf.: omnis insula est in circuitu vicies centena millia passuum,: caelum,: corpus intenditur,: sanguinem suum omnem profundere,every drop of, all,: omnis in hoc sum,I am wholly engaged in this,.—With plur. verb: omnis Graecia decoravere, etc., Cat. ap. .—As subst.: omne, is, n., every thing: nos autem, ab omni quod abhorret ab oculorum auriumque adprobatione, fugiamus,—Hence, adv.: omnīno, q. v.

la:adv:omnino.gloss: in all things, in all ways, entirely, utterly, altogether, wholly
senses: in all things, in all ways, entirely, utterly, altogether, wholly
in any thing, in any way, at all
la:adv:omnino.html:
omnīno, adv.
omnis
.
In gen., altogether, wholly, entirely, utterly, at all (syn.: prorsus, penitus): Neoptolemus apud Ennium philosophari sibi ait necesse esse, sed paucis: nam omnino haud placere, entirely, i. e. constantly, ; v. also ( Vahl.): non omnino jam perii: est reliquom quo peream magis,: defensionum laboribus aut omnino aut magnā ex parte liberatus,: ut non multum aut nihil omnino Graecis cederetur,not at all,: ita fit ut omnino nemo esse possit beatus,: id agimus ut id in sapiente nullum sit omnino,; cf. : Clodium sanxisse, ut vix aut omnino non posset ... infirmari sua lex,not at all,: non omnino quidem, sed magnam partem,: quae aut omnino aut certe facilius consequentur,: eos omittamus, qui omnino nusquam reperiuntur,: causas omnino numquam attigerunt,: non usquam id quidem dicit omnino, sed quae dicit idem valent, absolutely, i. e. expressly, explicitly, : omnino, quod cupis, efficies,: non tamen omnino Teucros delere paratis,: ne faciam, inquis, Omnino versus,: nihil omnino, te recitante placet,.— With omnis: non ego omnino lucrum omne esse utile homini existimo,all and every, of all kinds whatever,: hoc genus et cetera necessaria et omnino omnis argumentatio, etc.,: vis et injuria et omnino omne. quod obfuturum est,: sin omnino interierint omnia,; v. also the foll.—With prorsus: non justa, injusta, prorsus omnino obsequor,.—
In partic.
With numerals, in all, altogether, only, but, just (= οἱ πάντες): quinque omnino fuerunt,: diebus omnino decem et octo,: sane frequentes fuimus: omnino ad ducentos,: erant omnino itinera duo,there were only two ways,: duae omnino civitates,: cum omnino non essent amplius centum,: expeditionem unam omnino suscepit,: semel omnino eam viderat,.

24.—

In concessive clauses, by all means, indeed, doubtless, yes, certainly, to be sure. —With sed: restricti omnino esse nullo modo debemus, sed in deligendis idoneis judicium et diligentiam adhibere, etc.,: danda opera est omnino ... sed, etc.,; so : pugnas omnino, sed cum adversario facili,.—With autem: omnino est amans sui virtus ... ego autem non de virtute nunc loquor,.—
In making a statement of general application, in general, generally, universally: de hominum genere, aut omnino de animalium loquor,: plurimumque poëtis nostris, omninoque Latinis litteris luminis attulisti,; .—At the beginning of a general proposition: omnino fortis animus et magnus duabus rebus maxime cernitur,: omnino omnium horum vitiorum atque incommodorum una cautio est, ut, etc.,.—
After non modo (non), in a climax: non modo imperator, sed liber habendus omnino non est,: non modo tantam causam perorare, sed omnino verbum facere,: quos ego non modo reges appellatos, sed omnino natos nesciebam,; cf. .

la:verb:omitto.gloss: to let go, allow to pass by, let fall or let loose
senses: to let go, allow to pass by, let fall or let loose
to lay aside, give up, abandon, neglect or disregard
to omit, leave out (in speech or writing)
la:verb:omitto.html:
ŏmitto, īsi, issum, 3, v. a.
ob-mitto
,
to let go, let loose, let fall.
Lit. (rare; perh. not in Cic.; cf.: amitto, dimitto): aliquam,; : mulierem,: habenas,to let go,: arma,to let fall,: animam,to give up the ghost, to die,.—
Trop. (class.).
In gen., to lay aside, let go, give up, dismiss, neglect, disregard: omittere tristitiam,: iracundiam,: noxiam,to leave unpunished,: apparatum,: nec nostrae nobis utilitates omittendae sunt,: omitte timorem,lay aside,: voluptates,: omnibus omissis his rebus,laying aside all those things,: primam navigationem ne omiseris,do not neglect,: teneo quam optabam occasionem neque omittam,: hostes,: ducum officia,.—
In partic.
To pass over, say nothing of, omit, in speaking (cf., relinquo, praetereo): ut omittam cetera quae sunt innumerabilia,; cf.: ut alia omittam,: omitto illa vetera, quod, etc.,: innumerabiles viros,: de reditu,: de me,; .—
Of an action, to leave off, give over, cease doing any thing (syn. desino).—With inf.: iratus esse,. rogare, : lugere. : curare aliquid,: mirari,.—Hence, ŏmissus, a, um, P. a., negligent, heedless, remiss (ante-class.): animo esse omisso, Ter, Heaut. 5, 2, 9.—Comp.: ab re Omissior,in respect of property,.

la:adj:omnipotens.html:
omnĭpŏtens, ntis, adj.
omnis-potens
,
all-powerful, almighty, omnipotent (poet. and in post-class. prose), Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 202 Vahl.): Juppiter, id. ap. (Ann. v. 446 Vahl.); : pater,.—Absol.: arcuit omnipotens,; so, annuit omnipotens,: Neptunus, Turp. ap. : regina,i. e. Juno,: fortuna,: Juppiter,init.—Comp.: nam si ideo omnipotens Pater, qui Filium habet, omnipotentior ergo esse potuit, si plures haberet,.— Sup.: deus ille omnipotentissimus,; : creator, id. Civ. Dei, 21, 9.—Very freq. in eccl. Lat., with Dominus, Deus, etc.; and as subst.: Omnĭpŏtens, ntis, m., the Almighty: Omnipotens nomen ejus,: nec Omnipotens subvertet judicium, id. Job, 34, 12.—Hence, adv.: om-nĭpŏtenter, almightily, omnipotently, , 14, 27 init.

la:noun:omen.gloss: omen, sign, harbinger, portent, token (an object or occurrence believed to portend or predict a future event, circumstance, situation, or state of affairs)
senses: omen, sign, harbinger, portent, token (an object or occurrence believed to portend or predict a future event, circumstance, situation, or state of affairs)
la:noun:omen.html:
ōmen (old form osmen), ĭnis, n.
omen quod ex ore primum elatum est, osmen dictum, Müll.; cf.: osmen, e quo s extritum,, § 97: omen velut oremen, quod fit ore augurium, quod non avibus aliove modo fit, Fest. p 195 Müll.; perh. orig. osmen, for ausmen; root audio, that which is heard; hence, in gen.
.
Lit., any indication or action regarded as a foreboding, a foreboding, prognostic, sign, token, omen (class.; cf. prodigium): di te deaeque omnes faxint cum istoc omine,with your forebodings,: neque solum deorum voces Pythagoraei observaverunt, sed etiam hominum, quae vocant omina,. 102: ea quae divina testimonia vocant, ex responsis, oraculis, ominibus,: mi pater, inquit (filiola L. Pauli), Persa (catellus) periit. Tum ille Accipio, inquit, mea filia, omen, I take it as a good omen (of a victory over king Perses), : ingens omen magni triumphi,: qui discedens mecum ita locutus est, ut ejus oratio omen fati videretur,: quibus Antonius (o di immortales, avertite et detestamini, quaeso hoc omen!) urbem se divisurum esse promisit,; cf.: atque hoc quidem detestabile omen avertat Juppiter,; : exire malis ominibus,: quam (rem) tu ipse ominibus optimis prosequeris,: cum bonis ominibus incipere, Liv. praef. fin.: i secundo omine,go in God's name, good luck attend you,: impios parrae recinentis omen Ducat,: (Mater juvenem) Votis, ominibus et precibus vocat,: quod di prius omen in ipsum convertant,: quod acceperunt pro omine,.—
Transf.
A solemn assurance. condition. eā lege atque omine, ut, etc., .—
A solemn usage: hic sceptra accipere et primos attollere fasces Regibus omen erat,.—
Prima omina = nuptiae, as accompanied with auspices, ; cf.: Contineant nobis omina prima fidem, (4, 20, 14 M.).

la:adj:omniparens.gloss: that bears or produces all things; an epithet for deities
senses: that bears or produces all things; an epithet for deities
la:adj:omniparens.html:
omnĭpărens, tis, adj.
omnis-parens
,
all-bearing, all-producing (poet. and in post-class. prose); so, per terras omniparentes,: terra,; : dea Syria,, p. 213, 9 (but in , the correct read. is omnia parentis).

la:adj:omnigenus.html:
omnĭgĕnus, a, um, adj.
omnis-genus
,
of all kinds (poet. and in post-class. prose): omnigenūmque deūm monstra,: omnigenūm genitor deūm,: doctrinae, (but in ; Lachm. reads omne genus).

la:adj:omnimodus.gloss: of all or every sort or kind; omnimodous
senses: of all or every sort or kind; omnimodous
la:adj:omnimodus.html:
omnĭmŏdus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
of all sorts or kinds (post-class.). . 14: voculae,: gloria ejus. .

la:adv:omnimodo.gloss: By all means, in all ways
senses: By all means, in all ways
la:adv:omnimodo.html:
omnĭmŏdo (also written separate, omnī mŏdo), adv.
omnis-modus
,
by all means, in all ways, entirely, altogether, wholly (not ante-Aug.): evitemus omnimodo, ne deliberasse videamur,: non omnimodo res ea desperationem habet,; ; .

la:adj:ominosus.html:
ōmĭnōsus, a, um, adj.
omen
,
full of foreboding, portentous, ominous (post-Aug.): mons avibus obscenis ominosus, Messala ap. : res,. —Adv.: ōmĭnōsē, ominously: ominose retentus, Ps.-.

la:adj:omniformis.html:
omnĭformis, e, adj.
omnis-forma
,
of all shapes (post-class.): mundus receptaculum omniformium specierum, pp. 78, 98: machina, Prud. στεφ. 10, 339.

la:adj:omnipotentissimus.gloss: superlative degree of omnipotēns; the most omnipotent.
senses: superlative degree of omnipotēns; the most omnipotent.

la:adj:omnifarius.html:
omnĭfărĭus, a, um, adj.
omnis
,
of all sorts.—As adj. only in the gloss: omnifarius, παντοῖος, Gloss. Philox. (in , read omnifariam).—Hence, omnĭfărĭam, adv., on all sides, on every hand, everywhere, in every way (post-class. and rare): cum Oceanus omnes terras omnifariam et undiqueversum circumfluat,; ; .

la:adv:omnifariam.gloss: on all sides, everywhere, in all parts
senses: on all sides, everywhere, in all parts

la:verb:ominor.gloss: to forebode, presage, prognosticate, augur, predict, prophesy
senses: to forebode, presage, prognosticate, augur, predict, prophesy
la:verb:ominor.html:
ōmĭnor, ātus, 1, v. dep. (ante-class.
act. collat. form ōmĭno, āre: ut tibi bene sit, qui ominas, Pompon. ap. ) [omen], to forebode, prognosticate, to augur, presage, predict, prophesy (class.; syn.: divino, auguro, auspicor, vaticinor): malo (alienae) quam nostrae (rei publicae), ominari,: melius, quaeso, ominare,: felix faustumque imperium, : ac prope certā spe ominatos esse homines finem, etc.,: vera de exitu Antonii,: optamus tibi ominamurque in proximum annum consulatum,; cf.: clamor militum et sibi adversa, et Galbae prospera ominantium,wishing,.—Of things: naves cum commeatu rediere, velut ominatae ad praedam alteram repetendam sese venisse,as if they had divined, had had a presentiment,; cf. Weissenb. ad : male ominatis Parcite verbis,words of evil omen,.

la:verb:ominare.gloss: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of ōminor
senses: second-person singular present active imperative/indicative of ōminor

la:adj:omnivagus.html:
omnĭvăgus, a, um, adj.
omnis-vagus
,
roving everywhere, omnivagant: Diana,; Burm. dub. (al. omnivomus).
